requirements.title: Part 1: Setup
requirements.description: Create a marimo notebook; install pronouncing and the spaCy en_core_web_sm model; use the supplied readability_tools.py.
criteria: pronouncing and en_core_web_sm are available in the execution environment.
The instructor-provided readability_tools.py is available; its absence alone is not proof of missing student work.

requirements.title: Part 2: Find a text document
requirements.description: Choose fiction or nonfiction of at least 15,000 words.
criteria: Identify the chosen long document; fiction and nonfiction are allowed.
Verify at least 15,000 words in the actual analyzed text.

requirements.title: Part 3: Make predictions
requirements.description: Written predictions and reasoning before examining results. Source order cannot prove chronology.
criteria: Predict the difficulty of the chosen document.
Explain expectations about the ability to analyze reading difficulty.

requirements.title: Part 4: Measure difficulty
requirements.description: Load and segment the document, calculate reading difficulty, display at least four metrics, and discuss effectiveness and differences.
criteria: Document loading and segmentation are implemented.
At least FOUR different calculated difficulty methods are displayed; inspect actual outputs.
Written discussion addresses effectiveness and differences.

requirements.title: Part 5: Rank passages
requirements.description: Rank passages under chosen methods; inspect extremes and middle; discuss factors, effectiveness and differences; identify passages ranked differently between metrics.
criteria: Passages are ranked using chosen metrics.
High, low AND middle passages are inspected.
Written discussion explains factors used and their effectiveness.
Specific passages scored or ranked differently between metrics are identified.

requirements.title: Part 6: Discuss
requirements.description: Reflect on the process: challenges, what worked well, and what did not.
criteria: What did not work well is discussed.
